question: Temporary construction and maintenance signs are characterized by:
options: a:A red background with green writing.,b:An orange background with black writing.,c:A yellow background with blue writing.
note: Work zone and temporary signs use an orange background with black text or symbols to warn drivers.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what should you do with your lights?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on your parking lights.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers.
note: Turn on headlights anytime you cannot see other vehicles clearly so other drivers can see you as well.

question: When merging onto the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling you should:
options: a:Merge carefully into the gap.,b:Expect traffic to make room because you have the right-of-way.,c:Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.
note: Accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, and merge into the gap when it is safe; do not assume other drivers will yield for you.

question: If a school bus stopped ahead on the road has flashing lights and an extended stop arm, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Slow down to 10 mph and pass.
note: Stop and remain stopped while the bus is loading or unloading students and its red lights are flashing and stop arm extended; only proceed once those signals are off.

question: After stopping for a train and it passes, you should:
options: a:Wait for all signals to stop and look for a possible second train.,b:Proceed as soon as the visible train has passed without checking further.,c:Drive around the crossing gate if it seems clear.
note: Do not cross until gates are fully raised, warning lights have ceased, and you have checked for additional trains on other tracks.

question: When should you avoid using your horn?
options: a:To warn a driver who is not paying attention.,b:Near blind pedestrians.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.,d:If you might hit another vehicle.
note: Do not use the horn near someone who is blind; yield and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Why should motorists give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Because they have less developed reflexes and are smaller and harder to see.,b:Because they always follow traffic rules.,c:Because they are slower than adults and will not move suddenly.
note: Children on bicycles are less predictable and harder to see; give them extra room, especially near schools and parks.

question: When being tailgated by another driver, you should:
options: a:Create extra space ahead of your vehicle.,b:Increase your speed to pull away.,c:Brake suddenly to discourage them.
note: Allow more room in front of you and avoid sudden braking; change lanes if safe to do so or gradually slow to encourage the tailgater to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:You may during rush hour traffic.,b:If you entered the intersection on the green light.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:If you entered the intersection on a yellow light.
note: You may not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking it is not legal regardless of signal color or traffic conditions.

question: What is the definition of distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,c:Anything that forces evasive action by another vehicle.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that diverts eyes, hands, or mind from driving and contributes to collisions.

question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange signs, cones, and barriers indicate construction or maintenance work zones and require extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only your side mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, look over your shoulder to verify there is no vehicle in the blind spot before changing lanes.

question: What do curbs painted yellow or red typically indicate?
options: a:No parking or restricted parking zones.,b:Free parking areas.,c:Paid parking areas.
note: Painted curbs often signal parking restrictions: red commonly marks fire lanes; yellow may indicate loading zones or other restrictions.

question: Your vehicle's wheels have gone off the pavement. What is the first action you should take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.,c:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.
note: If your vehicle leaves the roadway, keep a firm grip on the wheel, take your foot off the gas, and gently use the brakes until your speed has dropped. When it is safe, check traffic and merge back onto the pavement—avoid sudden steering movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Move into another lane while inside an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Verify other drivers aren't entering the same lane.
note: Never change lanes within an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

question: If you approach a flashing yellow traffic signal, you should:
options: a:Treat the light like a stop sign.,b:Wait until the light turns green to proceed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution; no full stop is required unless necessary for safety.

question: You must yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
options: a:In a marked crosswalk.,b:In any crosswalk or intersection.,c:Crossing any street.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing any street; give pedestrians the right-of-way to enhance safety.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Someone or something unexpectedly entering your lane from between the parked cars.,b:All pedestrians to obey traffic laws.,c:Other drivers to respect your right-of-way.
note: When passing parked vehicles, watch for people opening doors, stepping out, or cars pulling out unexpectedly.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow indicate?
options: a:The protected left turn is about to end.,b:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow arrow warns that the protected left-turn period is ending and drivers must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using lights and siren?
options: a:Drive as close to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,b:Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Stop immediately even if you are in an intersection.
note: Pull right and stop clear of intersections; do not block an intersection or assume you should stop in its middle.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Driving in both directions may pass.,b:Next to the broken line may pass.,c:Next to the solid line may pass.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane means vehicles next to the broken line may pass; those next to the solid line may not.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow quick stops.,c:They are more maneuverable than passenger cars.
note: Large trucks require significantly more distance to stop than passenger vehicles due to their size and weight.

question: When is the proper time to adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you get into the car.,b:Whenever you need to use them.,c:Before you start driving.,d:After the vehicle is moving.
note: Adjust seat and mirrors and fasten your safety belt before moving the vehicle; do not wait until you are driving.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Beep your horn to warn them.,b:Expect the child to be in full control of the bike.,c:Expect the unexpected and drive cautiously.
note: Children on bicycles can behave unpredictably; slow down and be prepared for sudden movements.

question: If a child is about to run into the street ahead of you, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn to warn and deter the child.,b:Start to prepare to slow down without using the horn.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: If a pedestrian—especially a child—is about to enter your path, a sharp horn blast can alert them and help prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane must you make a left turn when leaving a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, start from the lane closest to the left curb and turn into the nearest legal lane.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Open a window.,b:Stop to rest or change drivers.,c:Drink coffee.
note: If tired, stop driving and rest or switch drivers—drowsiness slows reactions and impairs judgment.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Grasp the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop immediately.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, let the vehicle slow, and lightly apply the brakes when safe. Avoid sudden steering or heavy braking until speed is reduced.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the left.,b:Permitted from the right.,c:Not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed for traffic in either direction.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Broken yellow lines between opposing lanes mean drivers may pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver.,c:Only if pedestrians obey traffic signals.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether marked or unmarked, and stop if necessary to allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections with stop signs on all corners, who goes first?
options: a:The vehicle that arrived first at the intersection.,b:The vehicle that arrived last.,c:Drivers should always yield to other cars regardless of arrival order.
note: Vehicles proceed through four-way stops in the order of arrival; yield to any vehicle that arrived before you.

question: If you text while driving, how many times more likely are you to be in a crash than a non-distracted driver?
note: Texting while driving increases crash risk dramatically—about 20 times higher—because it diverts eyes, hands, and mind away from driving.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: High beams reflect off fog or mist back toward the driver, reducing visibility; use low beams instead.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas and avoid braking.,c:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly to regain traction.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road, gently ease off the accelerator and avoid braking until you regain traction.

question: What is the typical shape and color of construction zone signs?
options: a:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,b:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols; they are often diamond-shaped or rectangular to warn of roadwork.

question: You want to make a right turn, and a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the person with the guide dog has crossed before making your turn.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,c:Turn off your engine until they are across.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way; wait until they are safely across before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light is red but a police officer directs you to go through the intersection without stopping, you should:
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's direction and go through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: Police officers' directions take precedence over traffic signals; follow the officer's instructions.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of what?
options: a:Falling asleep at the wheel and causing a crash.,b:Missing an exit only.,c:Being late for appointments.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time and can lead to falling asleep while driving, which greatly raises crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you not do?
options: a:Back up on the roadway or shoulder to return to the exit.,b:Continue to the next exit and re-route.,c:Leave the freeway at the next exit and return safely.
note: Never back up on a freeway or shoulder; proceed to the next exit and find a safe route back.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid?
options: a:Driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Following far behind to reduce wind drag.,c:Driving on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have wide blind spots; avoid traveling alongside them for extended periods to remain visible to the driver.

question: If you're about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Releasing your seat belt.,b:Pressing your head against the head restraint.,c:Bracing yourself by pressing against the seat back.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace by pressing your back into the seat and head against the head restraint to reduce whiplash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns you to be alert and to slow down; proceed through the intersection only when it is safe.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Only slow down if you see ice.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Drive at the posted speed.,d:Speed up to avoid hydroplaning.
note: Wet, snowy, or icy surfaces reduce tire traction; slow down and increase following distance to maintain control.

question: What is the term used for the amount of alcohol in a person's bloodstream?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream; higher BAC indicates greater impairment.

question: When driving at night you should:
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Night driving reduces visibility and depth perception; increase following distance and use headlights correctly (low beams when appropriate).

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To keep your engine warm.,d:To improve fuel economy.
note: Headlights increase your vehicle's visibility to other drivers in low-visibility weather; if wipers are required, low beams must also be used.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, which actions are required?
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors, and signal your intention.,b:Only signal and then change lanes.,c:Check mirrors but don't signal if traffic is light.
note: Always use your signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to verify blind spots before moving laterally.

question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, you should use:
options: a:Fog lights only.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams will reflect back and impair vision.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction on a wet road, you should:
options: a:Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to stop sliding.,c:Slow down gradually without applying the brakes.
note: If you start to hydroplane, ease off the gas and slow gradually without braking until tires regain contact with the road.

question: If you start feeling drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Try to fight it until you reach your destination.,b:Take a break to rest or change drivers.,c:Take caffeine pills to stay awake.
note: If drowsy, stop at a safe location to rest, nap, or switch drivers rather than trying to push on.

question: What can happen if you mix a prescription drug with alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Many legal medications can impair driving ability, and combining them with alcohol may increase impairment and make you unfit to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: Maintain speed and position to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter traffic safely once it is clear to do so.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: Reduce speed before entering curves or intersections; braking on a curve increases the risk of skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If no signs or markings control turns at an intersection, you should turn into which lane?
options: a:Into the first available lane.,b:Into any lane.,c:Into the last available lane.
note: When there are no lane-control markings, turn into the first legal lane in your direction of travel and avoid changing lanes during the turn.

question: If you approach an intersection at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,c:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal will turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: If you see pedestrians waiting to use a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:Pull to the right and go around them.,c:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until they have cleared the road before proceeding.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at the same speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: Deal with one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian only if it is safe to do so.

question: When following a motorcycle you should:
options: a:Allow a larger following distance than you would for a car.,b:Be ready to use your horn frequently.,c:Drive more slowly than usual.
note: Motorcycles can stop or swerve quickly; a three- to four-second following distance gives time to react.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always stop no matter what.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A pentagonal school crossing sign warns to be alert for children and prepare to slow or stop as needed.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually and use the brakes lightly when needed.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: Grip the wheel, lift off the accelerator to slow, and apply the brakes gently once the vehicle has slowed to regain control and steer to a safe spot.

question: What does a 'No passing zone' sign indicate?
options: a:It is not safe and not legal to pass in this area.,b:You should speed up slightly.,c:You should maintain a steady speed.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign indicates that passing is prohibited because visibility or road conditions make passing unsafe.

question: A double solid yellow centerline indicates what about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates no passing from either direction.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch to high beams to see better.,c:Flash your lights repeatedly.
note: Avoid looking directly at blinding headlights; look toward the right edge of the road and use peripheral vision to stay oriented.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: Use your right foot for both the gas and brake to maintain smooth, controlled braking and acceleration.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol depresses the central nervous system, impairing judgment, reaction time, and coordination.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Appropriate in bad weather, but often a hazard when done unnecessarily.,b:Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.,c:Always a safe defensive technique.
note: Driving much slower than other traffic on a clear road can create frustration and risky passing maneuvers that increase crash risk.

question: Which of the following is a recommended safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beam lights in fog.,b:Staring at the road directly ahead for long periods.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
note: To stay aware of hazards, scan the road and check your mirrors every few seconds rather than staring straight ahead.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,b:Quickly turn inside the truck to beat it to the corner.,c:Squeeze between the truck and curb to make your turn.
note: Large vehicles require extra space to turn; do not try to pass between them and the curb—wait until they complete the turn.

question: If another vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, what is the first response you should take?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Swerve into the lane next to you.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: Remove pressure from the accelerator to increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead without braking or swerving abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:The speed you choose does not affect safety.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can be hazardous by causing other drivers to make risky passing maneuvers; keep pace with traffic within posted limits.

question: Drivers must obey instructions from which persons in construction areas?
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons).,b:Security guards in parking lots.,c:Drivers who are broken down on the roadway.
note: Flaggers control traffic flow and must be obeyed to protect both workers and drivers in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being tailgated on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.,c:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
note: If you cannot change lanes, gradually reduce speed to encourage the tailgater to pass rather than engaging in risky maneuvers.

question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of freeway traffic.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At the posted legal speed even if traffic is slower.
note: Match the speed of freeway traffic when safe and legal so you can merge smoothly into the flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May drivers pass another vehicle using the shoulder of the road?
options: a:When the shoulder is paved.,b:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Never use the shoulder to pass another vehicle; it is unsafe and other drivers won't expect you there.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to remove alcohol; coffee, food, or showers do not speed the elimination of alcohol.

question: Alcohol, in any concentration, is:
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows nerve impulses and impairs concentration and alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From where should you begin a left turn when turning from a two-way street?
options: a:On the left of the centerline.,b:Near the centerline.,c:Near the right-hand side of the road.
note: When making a left turn from a two-way street start from the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the first available legal lane of the new road.

question: Which commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.
note: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions is a common factor in crashes; maintain safe speed for conditions.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: Parking uphill with a curb, point the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Any amount of alcohol can impair driving ability; even a single drink affects coordination and judgment.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.,c:Blind spots can be checked by using only your rearview mirrors.
note: Mirrors do not remove blind spots; large trucks have substantially larger blind areas that other drivers should avoid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow displayed for your lane, when may you proceed?
options: a:When you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:Only after the arrow changes to green with no other signal.
note: A green arrow gives you the right to proceed in the arrow's direction from the corresponding lane when the way is clear.

question: Why is driving at night more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road surface is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from other vehicles mean you cannot see as far ahead at night; use headlights and drive with caution.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some cough/cold medications.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only prescription medications.
note: Many substances—including sedatives, tranquilizers, marijuana, and over-the-counter cough or cold medicines containing antihistamines or codeine—can impair driving.

question: Which action can help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Use your horn frequently to express frustration.
note: Signaling lane changes and driving courteously reduces misunderstandings and helps prevent road rage.

question: Why is it dangerous to make sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot see large vehicles in their mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses require longer stopping distances than passenger cars.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than cars.
note: Because of their size and weight, large vehicles need much more distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them increase collision risk.

question: On gravel or dirt roads, your tires:
options: a:Have less traction than on pavement, so slow down.,b:Grip the road better than on pavement.,c:Provide better visibility than on pavement.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping and skidding risk; reduce speed and drive cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are facing a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: Never enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking the intersection on a green light can lead to a citation and safety issues.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making left turns must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,b:Passing cars only.,c:No specific vehicles.
note: Vehicles making left turns must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicycles and motorcycles, that are going straight or turning right.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches, you should:
options: a:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Continue driving but stay out of its way.,c:Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
note: State law requires motorists to pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for approaching emergency vehicles using lights and siren.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.,b:Cautiously pass at 10 mph or slower.,c:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk; pedestrians may be crossing that you cannot see. Wait until pedestrians are clear.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent typically does what to crash risk?
options: a:Has no effect on driving.,b:Won't put other drivers at risk.,c:Nearly doubles your chances of being in a fatal crash.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly increase crash risk; each 0.02 percent increment nearly doubles the odds of a fatal crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to perform before making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions and adjust your speed as needed.,b:Always move to the left lane before turning.,c:Increase your speed right before the turn.
note: Look to the rear and both sides for traffic, signal, and slow to a safe speed before turning.

question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light turns to yellow, you should:
options: a:Stop.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Increase your speed to avoid an accident.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed to clear the intersection safely.

question: Slowing down just to look at a crash or other unusual event typically:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow.
note: "Rubbernecking" creates congestion and increases the risk of secondary crashes; remain focused and keep moving safely.

question: What is the only thing that will reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.,d:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing speeds up the process.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for making a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.,b:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,c:Approach in the lane nearest the right curb, then move toward the middle before turning.
note: Signal and approach from the lane nearest the curb, staying as close to the right edge as practical before turning.

question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Clear snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors so you have unobstructed visibility in all directions.

question: Why should you leave extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers when they want to slow down.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop. Do not pull in front of a truck and then brake; allow extra space for its stopping distance.

question: A broken yellow centerline on the roadway means what regarding passing?
options: a:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted at any time.
note: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means you may cross the centerline to pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what is the proper procedure?
options: a:Select a safe gap in traffic and merge smoothly into the lane.,b:Always stop on the ramp before entering the highway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once to speed up.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and then merge into a safe gap without stopping unless absolutely necessary.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign, you must:
options: a:Stop.,b:Slow.,c:Turn.
note: An octagonal sign always means STOP; come to a complete stop, yield as required, and proceed only when safe.

question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards earlier and anticipate changes in traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic speed.
note: Looking farther ahead on high-speed roads allows you to detect hazards sooner and plan lane changes or speed adjustments.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, you must do what?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to vehicles approaching from your right.
note: At a yield sign you must slow or stop if necessary and give right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles close enough to cause a conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Judge distance and speed of oncoming vehicles before passing.,b:Sound your horn while passing.,c:Flash headlights to signal your pass.
note: Ensure ample time and space to pass and be confident about oncoming traffic speed and distance before moving into the opposing lane.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More sober.,c:More coordinated.
note: Higher BAC corresponds to greater impairment of judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to the lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to enter a freeway, how should you check for traffic?
options: a:Use your rearview and side mirrors only.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to check blind spots.
note: When merging, use mirrors and shoulder checks to confirm there is space and to see vehicles in your blind spots.

question: What can continuous hard braking on snow and ice cause?
options: a:Locking of the front wheels and loss of steering control.,b:Faster stopping, reducing crash risk.,c:Prevention of brakes from freezing.
note: Hard continuous braking on slippery surfaces can lock the wheels and eliminate steering control. Maintain a slower speed and brake gently.

question: When backing up, you should:
options: a:Look through the rear window while reversing.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Press the gas gently to control movement.
note: Turn and look through the rear window when backing; drive in reverse at low speed and do not depend solely on mirrors or cameras.

question: Under low-visibility conditions due to fog, you should:
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Increase your speed so you clear the area quickly.
note: In fog, use low beams and reduce speed; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely and wait.

question: You should always travel at:
options: a:The speed of vehicles surrounding you.,b:The posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:A speed appropriate for the road and weather conditions.
note: Drive at a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions, staying within legal limits.

question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: Reducing speed on wet roads helps prevent hydroplaning; avoid sudden steering or braking inputs when traction is reduced.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is worn, it can cause:
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes only.,c:Steering slack only.
note: Bad suspension affects vehicle handling and control and should be repaired to maintain safe steering and stability.

question: Which of the following is a dangerous driving habit in work zones?
options: a:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers/machines.,b:Tailgating another vehicle only.,c:Failing to carefully watch for workers and equipment only.
note: In work zones reduce speed, avoid tailgating, and remain alert for workers and moving equipment to reduce crash risk.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean passing across the centerline is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving. It is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that affects driving ability.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:At all times; do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian.,b:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if traffic signals favor the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield and take any action necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian regardless of the pedestrian's compliance with traffic laws.

question: Which statement best describes a driver license?
options: a:Requirement.,b:Privilege, not a right.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted under the law, not an inherent right; it must be earned and maintained.

question: Upon seeing orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,c:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,d:Ignore the signs and cones.
note: Work zones warn of workers, slow equipment, or closed lanes; reduce speed and be prepared to slow or stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after stopping?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.,b:When you are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.,c:Whenever you yield to traffic.
note: After a full stop you may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless signs prohibit it.

question: How do sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,b:They only affect large vehicles.,c:They only cause visibility problems.
note: Strong winds can reduce visibility and physically move vehicles, creating hazards for cars, trucks, motorcycles, and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:After about three seconds.
note: Return to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating you have enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Never stop when approaching a yield sign.
note: Approach a yield sign prepared to stop and give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lane you intend to enter if it is close enough to be a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.,b:Slow down.,c:Check the inside rearview mirror.
note: Check mirrors and glance over the appropriate shoulder to verify your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: If you encounter a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to them.,b:Expect them to yield to you.,c:Honk to warn them of your presence.
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians have the right-of-way; always yield and be extra cautious around them.

question: Why is night driving more challenging?
options: a:Because it is harder to judge distance and the speed of other vehicles in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are fewer cars on the road at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night limits how far you can see—often only as far as your headlights—and makes it harder to judge distance and speed.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what is required of drivers?
options: a:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When a bus displays stop signals while loading or unloading, all motorists must stop until children are clear and the bus resumes motion.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because drivers often pull behind large vehicles before passing.,c:To avoid being caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large vehicles can block your view and have large blind spots; leaving extra space lets you see around them and react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Changing lanes from one lane to another should be done:
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Change lanes only when necessary, signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots; do so gradually and carefully.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no safety barrier, you should:
options: a:Quickly cross if it looks like you can beat the train.,b:Assume no trains cross there.,c:Cross only after looking both directions for an oncoming train.
note: At crossings without barriers, always look both ways and stop if a train is approaching; never try to outrun a train.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
note: If you damage parked property and the owner can't be found, leave a note with contact information securely attached to the vehicle.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery during rainfall?
options: a:Just after the rain begins.,b:After it has been raining several hours.,c:After one to two hours of rain.
note: When rain first starts, accumulated oil and dirt on the pavement mix with water to create a greasy, slippery surface.

question: Why are roads often more hazardous right after it begins to rain?
options: a:Because you should avoid making fast turns or stops until road traction improves.,b:Because tire traction is improved so you can drive faster.,c:Because visibility is always worse than during a heavy downpour.
note: Oil and residues on the pavement mix with early rain to create slick surfaces, so slow down and avoid abrupt maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic while your light is green, what is the best action?
options: a:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,b:Partially enter the intersection to establish right-of-way.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot.,b:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the side mirror.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot in the direction you intend to move in addition to checking mirrors.

question: On a slippery road, how should your following distance compare to normal?
options: a:Maintain a greater distance from the vehicle ahead than normal.,b:Keep the same following distance as normal.,c:Follow closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: Slippery roads require longer stopping distances, so increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:Regulatory signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Orange signs are commonly used for highway work zones and warn drivers of construction or maintenance activities ahead.

question: When driving in heavy fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog to reduce reflected glare; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road and wait.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which sign indicates when it is safe to return to your lane after passing?
options: a:You have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:You cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,c:You see the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: Only return to the lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection means you should do what?
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop, then enter when safe.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to proceed with caution and be prepared to yield to traffic or pedestrians as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:The same as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, then proceed only when the way is clear, similar to a stop sign.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, what is the safest action?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up.
note: Avoid confrontation—yield or get out of the aggressive driver’s way to reduce the risk of an incident.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Play loud music so you won’t think about your argument.,d:Call someone while driving to calm down.
note: Emotions affect driving ability; calm down and regain focus before operating a vehicle.

question: Which color is most commonly used for regulatory signs?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers specific laws and controls (direction, speed, lane use, parking). They are commonly white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

question: How should you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy weather?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Lower your speed in wet conditions to reduce the chance your tires will ride on a water layer and lose traction.

question: Which of the following describes how alcohol and drugs affect driving skills?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:Driving ability is unaffected.,c:All of the above.,d:Alertness and concentration.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol depress the nervous system, reducing alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination.

question: What is the best practice to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Always keep your eyes focused only ahead of your car.,c:Turn off the radio.
note: Constantly scan front, sides, and rear so you can detect hazards early and adjust speed or position as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arkansas, what are shared center lanes used for?
options: a:To make left turns from either direction.,b:To accelerate after turning left only.,c:To pass slower traffic.
note: Shared center turn lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and should not be used as acceleration or passing lanes.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road that has no curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road.,c:Left, toward the center of the road.
note: When parking downhill on a road without a curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: You should allow an extra cushion of space when following which driver?
options: a:A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (such as truck/bus pulling trailer).,b:A station wagon.,c:A small passenger car.
note: Large vehicles or those towing trailers may lack rear visibility and require a greater following distance to avoid hazards and see around them.

question: Tailgating, or following another vehicle too closely, can:
options: a:Cannot result in a traffic citation.,b:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,c:Is required when traffic is heavy.,d:Reduce collisions by preventing being cut off.
note: Tailgating encourages aggressive driving and increases crash risk; it may also lead to legal penalties.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance at night to allow more time to react when visibility is reduced.

question: Which part of the roadway is most likely to become icy in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: Shaded areas often freeze before and thaw after the rest of the road, making them more likely to be icy.

question: What does a steady red arrow displayed on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Drivers may not proceed in the indicated direction until the arrow changes.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,c:Drivers may proceed in the indicated direction with caution.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the arrow's direction; wait for a green signal to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or without signaling.,b:Check for other vehicles moving into the same space.,c:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: Avoid sudden or un-signaled lane changes; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway.,c:Stop where you are.
note: If your vehicle is disabled, you should, if possible, pull completely off the main traveled portion of the road with all wheels off the pavement.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct action?
options: a:When safe, gradually steer back onto the roadway.,b:Turn immediately back onto the roadway.,c:Stop immediately.
note: Do not jerk the wheel back onto the pavement. Slow down, check traffic, and ease the vehicle back onto the road when it is safe.

question: Prior to entering a curve, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Brake hard into the curve.
note: Slow to a safe speed before entering a curve; braking while turning can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers obey posted speed limits?
options: a:Only in heavy traffic.,b:Only when police officers are present.,c:At all times.
note: Obey posted speed limits at all times and check your speedometer frequently to remain within the limit.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, you should:
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stare at the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: Glance slightly to the right to avoid direct glare, then use peripheral vision to monitor the oncoming vehicle's position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When it comes to right-of-way, a driver should:
options: a:Assume all drivers will obey right-of-way rules automatically.,b:Assume most drivers obey the rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid a collision.
note: Even if you have the right-of-way, be prepared to yield or take evasive action to prevent a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling next to the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Signal both when you are pulling toward the curb and when leaving the curb to inform other road users of your actions.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You are required to carry evidence of financial responsibility and show proof of insurance upon request after a traffic stop or collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, you should:
options: a:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,b:Always maintain your position.,c:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
note: When traffic permits, create space to allow vehicles to merge safely into your lane.

question: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot across a sidewalk, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield and only stop if they are blocking your path.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
note: Drivers must stop before entering the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians already using it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, to whom should you yield?
options: a:Yield to any driver who arrived before you.,b:Yield to the driver on your left.,c:Yield to the vehicle across from you.
note: Vehicles proceed through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If one arrived before you, yield to that vehicle.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid temporary blindness from oncoming high beams and keep your vehicle on course.

question: What does double solid yellow centerline signaling mean?
options: a:Neither direction may pass.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass only.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: Is it lawful to drive while impaired by medication that affects your ability to drive?
options: a:No — driving while impaired by medication is not permitted under any circumstances.,b:Yes if the medication was prescribed by a physician.,c:Yes if you do not feel drowsy.
note: Driving under the influence of any substance that impairs your ability to drive—including prescribed or over-the-counter medications that affect alertness—is illegal and dangerous.

question: When stopped at a red light that shows a green arrow in your direction, you may proceed if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the other lights change.,c:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: A green arrow gives a protected movement to proceed if you are in the correct lane and the way is clear, yielding to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than surrounding traffic, what is likely to happen?
options: a:You will most likely interfere with traffic and could be cited.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic may block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic and can result in a citation. Try to match the speed of traffic within the legal limit.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow beside a solid yellow means vehicles adjacent to the broken line may pass; those next to the solid line may not.

question: A stopped school bus with red flashing lights means you must:
options: a:Stop and proceed when you think children are clear.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.,c:Remain stopped while the red lights flash.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, approaching drivers must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing; exceptions apply on divided highways.

question: Which action helps prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning results from driving too fast on wet pavement—reducing speed is the primary prevention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: There are two lanes moving in your direction and you are in the left lane while vehicles are passing you on the right. If a driver behind wants to go faster, what should you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane when it is safe to do so.,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.,c:Stay in your lane and not impede traffic.
note: If it is safe, move to the right lane to allow faster traffic to pass; the left lane is typically used for passing and faster travel.

question: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to alert them to your presence.,b:Allow them the right-of-way.,c:Quickly swerve around them.
note: Pedestrians using white canes or guide dogs must be given absolute right-of-way; do not honk or swerve around them.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should:
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid blinding the driver ahead and to increase safety.

question: When adjusting your inside rearview mirror, you should position it so you can see:
options: a:The entire rear window.,b:The passengers in the backseat clearly.,c:Your own reflection for visibility.
note: Adjust the mirror so you can view the entire rear window with minimal head movement from the driver's seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Speed up.,c:Maintain a constant speed.
note: When being passed, do not speed up or interfere with the passing vehicle; maintain a steady speed to allow a safe pass.

question: Like alcohol or drugs, drowsiness can do what to your driving?
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Help you be a better driver.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Lack of sleep reduces alertness, slows reaction time, and impairs judgment similar to alcohol or drugs.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, you should:
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: If no one is injured and the vehicle can be safely moved, remove it from the traffic lane to avoid creating a hazard.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street, what must you do?
options: a:Do not have to stop for them.,b:You must stop for them.,c:Proceed as usual.,d:Sound your horn to warn them.
note: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are not using a crosswalk.

question: What should you do when driving in fog?
options: a:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.,b:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog and reduce speed; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the roadway and wait until it clears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
note: If a clear view of cross traffic is obscured, stop and inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

question: If the centerline is a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: If the broken line is on your side, you may pass; if the solid line is on your side, passing is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering a freeway?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Merge into a different lane when possible.,c:Slow down only and stay in your lane.
note: If possible, change lanes to create a gap for entering traffic; otherwise adjust your speed to allow safe merging.

question: What do yellow center lines separate?
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.
note: Yellow center lines mark the separation between opposing directions of traffic on two-way roads; solid vs. broken indicates passing rules.

question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,b:Not drive through it; turn around and find another route.,c:Slam on the brakes.
note: Never attempt to drive into flooded areas; even shallow water can hide hazards and may wash your vehicle away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When would it be illegal to start across an intersection?
options: a:Allowed if you entered on a green light.,b:You must not enter if you'll block the intersection under any circumstances.,c:Allowed during heavy traffic.,d:It's permitted as long as you entered on a yellow light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely before the light turns red; blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

question: If an oncoming vehicle's high beams are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of your lane and avoid staring.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look toward the left edge of your lane.
note: Avoid looking directly at the bright lights; glance to the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to monitor the oncoming vehicle.

question: When crossing a sidewalk entering or exiting a driveway, drivers should:
options: a:Claim the right-of-way.,b:Yield to pedestrians.,c:Sound the horn to get pedestrians to move.
note: Drivers crossing sidewalks to enter or exit driveways must yield to pedestrians and may not drive on sidewalks except to cross them.

question: When a large truck ahead is making a right turn on a multi-lane street, the truck may:
options: a:Always stay in the right lane during the turn.,b:Have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Complete the turn in either lane with equal ease.
note: Long vehicles often swing wide when turning because the rear wheels track a shorter path than the front wheels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but cannot see a gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: If no space is available, reduce speed on the ramp and wait for a safe gap rather than stopping at the end of the ramp.

question: When must you obey a school crossing guard's directions?
options: a:At all times while they are directing traffic.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only if children are present.
note: Drivers must obey the instructions of school crossing guards whenever they are directing traffic near schools.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive the posted maximum speed limit only:
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed applies only under ideal road, traffic, and weather conditions; always adjust speed to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you give up your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often, even at controlled intersections.,b:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.
note: Yield your right-of-way whenever doing so helps avoid a collision—do not assume other drivers will always yield.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, you should:
options: a:Open a window and keep driving.,b:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine and continue driving.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, stop and rest or switch drivers rather than relying on caffeine or fresh air.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, how can you avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when traffic permits.,b:Slow down.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: When safe and traffic allows, move out of the right-hand lane to avoid conflicts with vehicles entering from on-ramps.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate what?
options: a:A school zone or school crossing.,b:A stop sign.,c:A regulatory sign.
note: Five-sided (pentagonal) signs are used to warn drivers of school zones and school crossings where children may be present.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or restrict the truck's ability to stop and maneuver.,b:Areas with several car lengths between vehicles.,c:Zones where it is safe to travel behind the truck.
note: "No zones" are dangerous blind spots and areas close to large vehicles where your presence may be unseen or restrict their maneuvering.

question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means to slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution—no full stop is required unless necessary.

question: On a multilane road where a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, who may pass?
options: a:Only traffic next to the dashed line may pass.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: Where a dashed line is adjacent to a solid line, only traffic on the dashed-line side may cross to pass when safe.

question: When you encounter a pedestrian carrying a white cane or using a guide dog, how must you respond?
options: a:Only if a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:Give them the right-of-way at all times.
note: Pedestrians using white canes or guide dogs (with or without a red tip) must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: What is the only medically proven way to reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up.,c:Take a cold shower to reduce BAC.
note: No food, drink, or activity speeds elimination of alcohol—only the passage of time lowers BAC.

question: To avoid injury from an airbag, how many inches should a driver sit from the steering wheel?
options: a:Approximately 10 inches.,b:About 20 inches.,c:About 15 inches.
note: Maintain about 10 inches from the center of the steering wheel to your chest to reduce the risk of airbag-related injuries.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Coordination.,b:Both alertness and coordination.,c:Alertness.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair multiple skills needed for safe driving, including alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to ten mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic regardless of flow.
note: Enter freeway traffic at or near the speed of vehicles already on the roadway to merge safely.

question: When can you legally go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When the warning lights are not flashing.,c:When you can clearly see both directions.
note: Do not go around or under any lowered crossing gate; wait until gates are fully raised and signals have stopped before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When completing a pass, you have enough room to return to the driving lane when:
options: a:The other driver signals for you to re-enter.,b:You look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to the driving lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Decrease as speed increases.,b:Remain unchanged.,c:Increase as speed increases.
note: Higher speed increases stopping distance and the potential severity of a collision; increase following distance when speeding.

question: When may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the centerline next to your lane is broken (dashed) and the way ahead is clear.,b:When you are on a hill or curve.,c:When there is a solid line next to your lane.
note: A broken (dashed) line beside your lane indicates passing is permitted when safe; solid lines prohibit passing.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and cross the intersection with caution; you do not need to stop unless required for safety.

question: As daylight begins to fade, to help others see you, you should use:
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on low beam headlights at dusk to increase your vehicle's visibility to other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight road with 500 feet clear view in both directions.
note: Never perform a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians.

question: If you refuse to take a lawful alcohol test when requested by an officer, what may happen?
options: a:You may lose your driver's license.,b:You are simply exercising your rights as a motorist.,c:There will be no consequences.
note: Refusing a lawful alcohol test can result in license suspension under implied consent laws and other penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling the same direction, how should you complete the maneuver?
options: a:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible, then return to your lane when safe.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,c:Pass as slowly as possible to minimize speed difference.
note: Pass decisively and return to the travel lane only when you have sufficient clearance and visibility to do so safely.

question: When a pedestrian is using a guide dog or carrying a white cane and is crossing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian.,b:Tell the pedestrian where to cross the street.,c:Only yield if you are at a corner.
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must always be given the right-of-way.

question: A pedestrian started after the 'Don't Walk' signal and is in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian has finished crossing before you proceed.,b:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,c:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
note: Even on a green light, you must yield to pedestrians who are in the intersection. Wait until they have crossed before you proceed.

question: When an oncoming car's headlights are very bright at night, you should:
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Avoid staring at oncoming headlights; look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes to avoid being blinded.

question: If a vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, how should you use it?
options: a:Wear both the lap and shoulder belt together.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: Both the lap and shoulder portions must be used for proper protection; using only one part greatly reduces safety.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which is an expected behavior?
options: a:They may wait on the side of the road.,b:They may use the left lane.,c:They may cut through all lanes.
note: Bicyclists are expected to ride with traffic and may use the left lane to make a left turn; expect them to behave like other vehicles when turning.

question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection and wait.,c:Pull to the center and stop until it passes.
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in an intersection, clear the intersection, then drive to the right and stop to allow it to pass.
