question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, what is the safest choice?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to drive through the water.,c:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.
note: Where possible, steer around deep puddles to avoid hydroplaning, loss of control, or vehicle damage.

question: In rainy weather you should be most cautious when turning or stopping:
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:One half hour after it stops raining.
note: The first half hour of rain mixes oil on the road with water, creating very slippery conditions—exercise extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive simultaneously from all directions, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on your right.,b:The vehicle on your left.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.
note: When multiple vehicles arrive at the same time without signals or signs, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When you see pedestrians near the roadway where you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Watch for pedestrians who might step into your path. Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along road edges or before intersections?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:They vibrate and make noise to warn inattentive drivers they've left the travel lane.
note: Rumble strips create sound and vibration to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the travel lane or approaching a stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If other drivers are passing you on both sides while you remain in the center expressway lane, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On roadways with four or more lanes of two-way traffic, remain in the right lanes unless you are passing or preparing to turn left; if you are driving slower than the flow of traffic, move to the right when safe.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap.,b:Turn up the radio to stay alert.,c:Increase your speed to arrive sooner.
note: If you experience drowsiness, stop at a safe location and rest; short naps can restore alertness and prevent crashes.

question: You are driving defensively when you:
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Only look at the car in front of you.,c:Keep your eyes moving to search for potential hazards.
note: Defensive driving involves constantly scanning the roadway and environment to anticipate hazards.

question: You must use low beam headlights any time you are:
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:On a freeway.,c:In fog.
note: Low beams reduce glare in fog and other low-visibility conditions; high beams can worsen visibility by reflecting back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which of these conditions?
options: a:At a red traffic light and when a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Only where there is a red traffic light.,c:Only when a stop sign is present.
note: Obey traffic control devices like red lights and the instructions of police officers directing traffic at all times.

question: What is the recommended placement of your hands to turn quickly and safely?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,c:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel to maintain control and perform safe turns, especially at higher speeds.

question: Holding a driver's license is considered a:
options: a:Requirement.,b:Privilege.,c:Right.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and can be suspended or revoked for unsafe or unlawful behavior.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Low beams improve visibility in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams can reflect back and worsen visibility.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should allow extra space in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:A station wagon stops more slowly.,b:A passenger vehicle requires more space.,c:Motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see.
note: Motorcycles can stop suddenly and are less visible, so leave extra following distance to allow room to react.

question: For drivers age 21 or older it is illegal to operate a vehicle with a BAC of at least:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Drivers 21 and older are legally impaired at a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher in Arkansas.

question: What is the first ability alcohol typically impairs?
options: a:Vision.,b:Judgment.,c:Balance.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making, which then leads to impaired vision and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles driving straight ahead.,b:No one; they have the right-of-way.,c:Only pedestrians, not vehicles.
note: A left-turning driver must yield to oncoming traffic and may not turn until the way is clear.

question: Arkansas law requires drivers to turn on headlights when:
options: a:They are driving closely behind another vehicle.,b:Windshield wipers are in use.,c:They want to get somebody's attention.
note: Headlights must be used when windshield wipers are needed due to weather; use low beams in rainy, snowy, or foggy conditions.

question: Which factor influences how a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:Weight.,b:Height.,c:Intelligence.
note: Alcohol absorption is influenced by weight, sex, food in the stomach, and how much has been consumed. Only time removes alcohol from the system.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur under which of these conditions?
options: a:Driving at the posted speed reduces risk.,b:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,c:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,d:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
note: A vehicle that travels much faster or slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of a crash.

question: If conditions are very foggy, you should slow down and:
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: In fog use low beams (and fog lights if equipped); high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: How far down the road should you look to avoid last-minute braking or turning?
options: a:About 15 seconds ahead.,b:About 3 seconds ahead.,c:About 10 seconds ahead.
note: Scan at least 15 seconds ahead to detect hazards early and allow time for safe adjustments; this gives following drivers more time to react.

question: Reaction time is likely to be slower after:
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol impairs reflexes and reaction time, making it harder to judge distances and respond to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, what should you see?
options: a:Both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Beep your horn to signal your move.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Only return to your lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating adequate clearance.

question: A dashed white line down the center of a roadway indicates what?
options: a:Lanes travel in the same direction and drivers may pass when safe.,b:Lanes travel in opposite directions and drivers may pass.,c:Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and permit lane changes and passing when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the green light.,c:Wait until vehicles have cleared before yielding to pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the intersection even when facing a green signal, especially when turning.

question: If bad weather reduces your visibility, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive faster to get off the road quicker.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead to allow more reaction time in poor visibility or slippery conditions.

question: What is the definition of a crosswalk?
options: a:Another name for a four-way intersection.,b:An area reserved for road construction workers.,c:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
note: A crosswalk is the portion of the roadway designated for pedestrian crossing; it may be marked or unmarked.

question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,b:Increase your speed to clear the zone quickly.,c:Maintain your normal speed throughout the zone.
note: Slow down, obey signs, and watch for workers and equipment; conditions can change quickly in work zones.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Use the brakes lightly and slow gradually.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and brake lightly to slow down gradually; avoid hard braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light should be treated as:
options: a:An indicator you are traveling the wrong way.,b:A stop sign (come to a complete stop),c:A signal you may not proceed until it turns green.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, the same as a stop sign.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Drive closer behind the truck than with a passenger vehicle.,b:Follow at a greater distance than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,c:Drive to the truck's right and wait to pass.
note: Large vehicles have bigger blind spots and greater stopping distances; maintain a larger following gap to improve visibility and safety.

question: What does a solid white center line mean on a roadway with lanes in the same direction?
options: a:Lanes travel in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes travel in opposite directions and drivers may pass.,c:Lanes travel in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; do not cross a solid line to pass or change lanes.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:You may pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:You may pass on the right when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross to pass on the left if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on its left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds have passed.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Only move back into the lane once you can clearly see the passed vehicle in your mirrors indicating adequate space.

question: Which statement about backing your vehicle is true?
options: a:Backing up is always potentially dangerous.,b:Backing up is dangerous only without a helper.,c:Backing up is only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing is inherently risky because visibility is limited; take extra care, use a helper if available, and back slowly.

question: If you've had several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is to:
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Wait several hours.,c:Drink several cups of coffee.
note: Only time allows the body to remove alcohol; other measures like coffee or showers do not speed elimination (about one hour per drink).

question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?
options: a:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.,b:As your speed increases, so should your following distance.,c:Both of the above.
note: Higher speed raises crash severity and increases stopping distances, so you should increase your following distance as speed rises.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic should yield to you.,c:You never have to yield when turning left.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians crossing the roadway before completing the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting the freeway onto a ramp that curves downhill, you should:
options: a:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve; braking in a curve can cause loss of control.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, you may:
options: a:Cross the centerline to change lanes when safe.,b:Must stay strictly within your lane.,c:Change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and permit lane changes and passing when safe.

question: What is the standard top-to-bottom order of traffic lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: Traffic lights are arranged red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom; observe them to control intersection movements.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When parked on a slope, turn the wheels to prevent the vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be parked within how many inches of the curb?
options: a:Six inches.,b:Twelve inches.,c:Eighteen inches.
note: When parallel parked, position your vehicle no more than 18 inches from the curb so it is visible and out of traffic flow.

question: How are fines for moving traffic violations in work zones typically handled in Arkansas?
options: a:Lessened.,b:Doubled.,c:Non-existent.
note: Fines for moving violations in work zones are doubled when workers are present and warning signs are posted.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel,b:A bridge,c:An intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed to cold air from all sides and can freeze before nearby pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When the driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,c:When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating sufficient space.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is sliding left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel left (in the direction of the skid).,b:Do not turn the steering wheel.,c:Turn the steering wheel right (opposite the skid).
note: When your rear skids left, steer left toward the skid to regain traction; take your foot off the accelerator and avoid braking unless necessary.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, you should:
options: a:Still wear seat belts.,b:Not wear seat belts because airbags are enough.,c:Wear seat belts behind your back for added protection.
note: Airbags are supplemental restraint systems; lap and shoulder belts must still be worn for best protection.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often, to know how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:Only when camback is necessary.
note: Frequently scanning mirrors keeps you aware of vehicles approaching from behind and helps you make safer decisions.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Put on your hazard lights and pull safely off the road.,b:Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.,c:Signal and move into the slow lane.
note: If possible, get your vehicle off the roadway away from traffic and turn on emergency flashers so other drivers know you are disabled.

question: Which of these is a sign of an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Having many passengers in the car.,c:Driving slowly.
note: Aggressive drivers often make unsafe lane changes and other unpredictable maneuvers; avoid engaging with them and get out of their way.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road.,c:Left, toward the center of the road.
note: When parking uphill or downhill on roads without curbs, turn wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if brakes fail.

question: What is a major consequence of excessive speed?
options: a:It increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.,b:It helps you maneuver around obstacles better.,c:Saves significant travel time.
note: Speeding is a leading factor in crashes and increases both the likelihood and severity of injuries and fatalities.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians must be yielded to by vehicles.,b:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,c:Construction workers must yield to vehicles.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in crossings and vehicles must stop for them unless traffic-control devices indicate otherwise.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you must:
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if no crosswalk is marked; stop and allow them to cross safely.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes especially important?
options: a:Turning on your headlights.,b:Looking well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Changing lanes frequently.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance; looking further ahead gives you more time to react to hazards.

question: A responsible driver should:
options: a:Stare directly in front of the car.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of the vehicle.
note: Good scanning includes watching to the sides, ahead, and behind to detect hazards early.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,c:Where signs and pavement markings permit passing.
note: Only pass where signs and pavement markings indicate passing is permitted and when you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, which statement is correct regarding yielding?
options: a:You must always yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield.
note: Drivers making left turns must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians who have the right-of-way before turning.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under in a vehicle with airbags?
options: a:The back seat.,b:The front seat.,c:The bed of a pickup truck.
note: Airbags are designed for adults and can be dangerous to young children; children age 12 and under should ride in the back seat.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed and signal your intentions early.,b:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: A steady speed and predictable signaling help the driver behind maintain a safe following distance.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down passing cars.,b:Sound your horn to get attention.,c:Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if safe to do so.
note: On high-speed interstates, turn on hazard lights, pull entirely off the roadway if possible, and remain in the vehicle for safety unless immediate danger requires otherwise.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:Alcohol impairs judgment, which is essential for safe driving.,b:If you are under the legal BAC limit, your driving is not impaired.,c:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it's safe to drive.
note: Alcohol affects decision-making and reaction time; even small amounts can impair the judgment needed for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which passing actions are unlawful?
options: a:Passing in a marked no passing zone or passing over a railroad crossing.,b:Passing only on the left when safe.,c:Passing on a road with a broken yellow centerline to your side.
note: You may not pass in marked no-passing zones, on hills or curves where visibility is limited, or over railroad crossings. These are illegal and unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:Both the ability to drive safely at higher speeds and constant alertness.,b:The ability to drive at increased speeds only.,c:Constant alertness only.
note: Interstate driving demands both alertness and the skill to safely operate at higher speeds and in faster traffic.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Follow closely because the trucker can see farther ahead.,c:Stay no more than one car length behind.
note: Trucks have large blind spots and require extra stopping distance; follow farther behind so the truck driver can see you and you have room to stop.

question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:
options: a:Vehicles.,b:Hazards.,c:Dangerous obstacles.
note: Bicycles are legally vehicles on roadways; bicyclists and motorists must obey the same traffic laws and share the road.

question: With oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Take a middle course between the oncoming traffic and the parked cars.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming traffic.
note: When faced with oncoming traffic on one side and parked cars on the other, position your vehicle in the center of your lane to maximize clearance on both sides.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem displayed on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:A slow-moving vehicle.,c:Shoulder work ahead.
note: The fluorescent orange-red triangle is used to identify slow-moving vehicles such as farm equipment or road maintenance vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid making?
options: a:That the other driver will make space for you to return to the lane.,b:That the other driver won't move.,c:That you can pass regardless of visibility.
note: Do not assume other drivers will create space; confirm it is safe to pass and return to the lane before doing so.

question: Which behavior tends to block the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,c:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
note: Rubbernecking—slowing to look at crashes or unusual events—causes congestion and should be avoided.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Pull over quickly.,b:Apply the brake and hold it.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake lightly.
note: Keep control by holding the wheel steady, ease off the accelerator, and apply the brakes gently. Pull off the roadway when safe.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true (repeat)?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,c:Blind spots can be seen in your rearview mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, blind spots remain; avoid lingering beside large trucks because of their extensive blind zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,b:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.,c:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.
note: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check behind you and also observe traffic ahead to ensure a safe gap.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Look for a way around lowered gates.
note: Railroad crossing warnings mean trains may be present; obey signs and signals and never go around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Yield only to pedestrians.,c:Yield only to cars already in the roundabout.
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the entry and to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain/snow, a good way to make sure other drivers see you is to:
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn up the instrument panel lights.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: Use headlights (low beams) when visibility is reduced so other drivers can see your vehicle.

question: If you park where vehicles don't normally park, what must you ensure?
options: a:That your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:That your reverse lights remain on.,c:That you park five feet from the curb.
note: Make sure your parked vehicle won't be a hazard by positioning it so other drivers can see it from any approach.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered distracting?
options: a:Because it occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind and diverts attention from driving.,b:Because it makes the driver worry about call costs.,c:Because it distracts other drivers.
note: Cell phone use while driving divides attention among hands, eyes, and brain, increasing crash risk even if hands-free.

question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, what should you do first?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Press down hard on the accelerator.
note: Before slowing or stopping, check mirrors to be aware of traffic behind you and avoid being struck from behind.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead on your side of the road with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the bus's red lights stop flashing.,b:Slow to 10 mph and proceed cautiously.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus has activated red flashing lights and its stop arm, traffic in both directions must stop until the lights are turned off and the arm is retracted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, a driver should look:
options: a:Only at the left outside mirror.,b:Over their left or right shoulder.,c:Only at the inside rearview mirror.
note: Look over the appropriate shoulder to see areas not covered by mirrors before changing lanes.

question: Before turning the ignition in a vehicle, what should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts and buckle your own.,b:Buckle your safety belt but not worry about passengers.,c:Start the engine and then advise passengers to buckle up.
note: Develop a routine of ensuring all occupants are properly belted before starting the vehicle. Seat belts should be fastened before ignition.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive relative to your headlights?
options: a:Slow enough so you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.,b:Use high beams all the time to see better.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright so others can see you.
note: At night you must drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.

question: Before entering an intersection, where should you look?
options: a:Left, then right, then left again.,b:Only to the left.,c:Only to the right.
note: Check left and right for approaching vehicles and pedestrians, looking left again since closer traffic often comes from that direction.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do about braking?
options: a:Stay off the brakes until you regain control.,b:Pump the brakes continuously.,c:Apply the brakes firmly immediately.
note: If the vehicle skids, remove your foot from the pedals and steer to regain control; braking can worsen the skid unless you have ABS.

question: How should you apply the gas pedal for safe control?
options: a:As quickly as possible.,b:Slowly and smoothly.,c:By lightly tapping.
note: Press the gas pedal gently and smoothly to avoid wheel spin or loss of control, especially on wet or slippery roads.

question: If conditions require you to have lights on, which should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, or snow; high beams can reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: When should you fasten your safety belt?
options: a:Before the engine is started.,b:Whenever you feel unsafe.,c:After reaching speeds over 45 mph.
note: Seat belts should be fastened before starting the engine; in most jurisdictions belt use is required by law.

question: What helps prevent you from becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax, concentrate on driving, and be realistic about travel time.,b:Tailgate the driver ahead of you.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit to get ahead.
note: Avoid taking other drivers' actions personally, plan extra travel time, obey speed limits, and remain calm to reduce the chance of becoming aggressive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?
options: a:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Do not attempt to change lanes within an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots beforehand.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection where the signal has just turned steady yellow and you have not entered yet, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop before the intersection.,b:Speed up to beat the light.,c:Reduce speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is about to turn red; if you can stop safely, do so rather than entering the intersection on red.

question: Which best describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They consider what other drivers might do and prepare to react.,b:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,c:They expect no breaks or courtesy from other drivers.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and adjust speed, position, and attention to reduce crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:All approaching vehicles.,b:Pedestrians waiting with a "Walk" signal.,c:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
note: When turning left you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any traffic with the right-of-way, including those on a pedestrian signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted and the tracks are clear.,b:Slow down and drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,c:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
note: It is illegal and dangerous to go around lowered gates. Stop behind the gates and wait until signals indicate it is safe to proceed.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you're stopping on snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Avoid using the brakes and let the car roll to a stop.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will pulse the brakes to maintain control.

question: Which of the following statements about work zones is correct?
options: a:Fines are the same as under normal conditions.,b:You must "Slow for the Cone Zone.",c:Only slow down if you think workers are present.
note: Drivers should slow down in work zones to protect workers and other road users; many areas have specific slow-for-the-cone-zone directives.

question: Any amount of alcohol in a driver's blood can impair what?
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Knowledge only.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect judgment, coordination, and the ability to drive safely, potentially leading to impairment.

question: In foggy conditions, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town with frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children.
note: Never stop on the tracks; if you cannot clear the tracks completely, wait until you can safely cross and clear the tracks.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, or railroad crossings you should always do what to check for hazards?
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles that seem stopped for no reason.,b:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,c:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
note: Whenever people may cross or traffic lines meet, look left and right to ensure no one or nothing is approaching your path.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.,b:Directly behind the cab only.,c:On the immediate left of the cab only.
note: Large trucks have extensive blind spots on both sides and directly behind; if you cannot see the driver in the truck's mirrors, the driver likely cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left (unless a sign prohibits the turn).

question: When driving in fog, which lighting should you use?
options: a:Four-way flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:No lights.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

question: If you continually pass other cars on a two-lane road by driving faster than the flow, what happens to your collision risk?
options: a:You increase your chances of a collision.,b:You get to your destination more quickly and safely.,c:You help prevent traffic congestion.
note: Frequent passing on two-lane roads raises your odds of a collision each time you maneuver to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to others, then proceed when safe.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield, and then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being followed too closely on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Speed up to match the speed of the car behind you.,b:Move into the lane to your right and let the other car pass.,c:Slow down to antagonize the driver.
note: If tailgated in the left lane, safely move to the right to let the faster driver pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After parking at a curb, when entering traffic you should:
options: a:Wait for a gap large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Enter the lane immediately and accelerate quickly.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then merge.
note: Merge only when you can reach the speed of traffic; accelerate in the gap rather than pulling slowly into moving traffic.

question: Should you always drive slower than surrounding traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and cause hazards.,b:Yes — it is always safer to drive slower.,c:Yes — it prevents collisions in all situations.
note: While slower speeds are necessary in poor conditions, driving excessively slowly can impede traffic and lead to citations or risky passing maneuvers.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:No parking, standing, or stopping.,b:Loading zone.,c:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.
note: Red curb paint means you may not stop, stand, or park in that area.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure about your vehicle position?
options: a:Your vehicle is entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Stay in the same lane since the motorcycle occupies less space.,c:Sound your horn to force the rider to the shoulder.
note: Allow a full lane width to the motorcycle when passing and complete the pass only when your vehicle is fully in the left lane.

question: What do broken yellow centerlines indicate?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic; dashed yellow lines indicate passing is permitted when safe.

question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed in which situation?
options: a:Driving in long, gradual curves.,b:Driving down long, gradual hills.,c:Driving up long or steep hills.,d:When traveling on flat open roads at high speed.
note: Heavy vehicles require more time to accelerate and often slow when climbing long or steep grades; allow extra space behind trucks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.,b:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,c:Use cruise control when approaching a railroad crossing.
note: Follow signs, flaggers, and warning signals at railroad crossings. Stop when directed to do so for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection permits you to:
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection.,b:Adjust your mirrors while passing through.,c:Proceed through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.
note: A green light means you may go, but you must yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection and proceed only when it is clear.

question: When driving in a work zone, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Avoid tailgating and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,c:Pass the driver in front as soon as you can.
note: In work zones, increase following distance and avoid tailgating to allow space from barriers, equipment, workers, and other vehicles.

question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane. What should you do?
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.,b:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.,c:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
note: Even without a marked crosswalk, yield to pedestrians and stop if necessary to let them finish crossing the roadway.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is directly behind you on a city street, you should:
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles with lights and sirens by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until they pass; if in an intersection, clear it and then stop.

question: Excessive speed often leads to:
options: a:No increased crash risk.,b:Improved ability to react to hazards.,c:High-risk decision-making and increased crash risk.
note: Driving too fast increases the chance of crashes and leads to risky decisions rather than saving time.

question: If heavy smoke covers the roadway ahead, what is the safest immediate response?
options: a:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on high beam headlights and continue driving.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
note: If visibility is severely reduced by smoke, slow down and stop off the road in a safe spot until conditions improve.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you not do?
options: a:Brake abruptly or heavily.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to control the skid.,c:Brake lightly.
note: Avoid braking hard during a skid as it can make the situation worse; instead, ease off the controls and steer to regain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a green arrow, you must:
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield only to pedestrians in the intersection.
note: A green arrow gives you the right to go in the arrow direction after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: When you notice animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop in the lane and exit your vehicle.,d:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: Slow down and move forward cautiously; animals may bolt or there may be more out of sight, so give them space and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, after checking mirrors you should also:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Always slow down in your current lane.
note: Look over your shoulder to verify the lane next to you is clear before signaling and changing lanes.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind your vehicle?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out the back window regularly.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: Regularly scanning your rearview mirror helps you remain aware of traffic conditions behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop you and a driver on your left arrive at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You have the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn goes first.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; if the other vehicle is on your left, you proceed first.

question: On slippery surfaces such as snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Shift to a low gear before descending steep hills.,b:Follow other vehicles more closely to maintain traction.,c:Pump the brakes continually to prevent freezing.
note: To reduce skidding on slippery grades, select a low gear before going down steep hills and increase following distance; pump brakes only if you lack ABS.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Time — allowing your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drinking caffeine such as coffee.,c:Eating high-fat foods.
note: Time is the only proven method to lower BAC; other remedies like coffee or food do not speed elimination.

question: When taking any medication, what should you do if you plan to drive?
options: a:Have someone follow you home.,b:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,c:Consult your doctor about effects before driving.
note: Ask your doctor or pharmacist how any prescription or over-the-counter medicine might affect your driving ability.

question: Blue highway signs typically provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services (e.g., food, rest areas).,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage and distances to locations.
note: Blue signs are service signs used to indicate facilities like rest areas, hospitals, and food services.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is correct about checking for traffic before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and over your left for a left lane change.,b:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,c:You don't need to check any blind spots if you have two outside mirrors.
note: Always check mirrors and then look over the appropriate shoulder to verify no vehicle or bicycle is in your blind spot.

question: Who may use marked handicap parking spaces?
options: a:Anyone if other spaces are full.,b:Only drivers with the appropriate license plate or hanging tag.,c:People who feel unwell but have no placard.
note: Handicap spaces are reserved for persons with disabilities who display the proper plate or placard showing the international symbol of accessibility.

question: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
note: When you see an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, safely pull to the right edge of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are harder to see, you should:
options: a:Make constant visual checks for them.,b:Share a lane with them when convenient.,c:Always slow to a stop when one is nearby.
note: Continuously scan for small vehicles and check your blind spots to avoid missing a motorcycle or scooter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you enter a left-turn lane with oncoming traffic present, you should:
options: a:Signal well before you reach the intersection.,b:Turn your front wheels left to be ready for the turn.,c:Move to the left of the center lane before turning.
note: Signal at least 100 feet before turning and keep wheels straight until you begin the turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

question: When driving on snow or ice, you should make speed and directional changes:
options: a:More gradually than usual.,b:Using cruise control for stability.,c:The same as normal conditions.
note: On slippery surfaces make gentle steering and speed adjustments; never use cruise control on snow or ice.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Ease up on the gas pedal and steer in the direction of the skid.,b:Brake as hard as possible to stop quickly.,c:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: Remove pressure from the accelerator or brake, then steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go to recover control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up to match traffic.,b:Use the main road shoulder to accelerate to traffic speed.,c:Accelerate and merge only after you identify a safe gap in traffic.
note: On short ramps without acceleration lanes, wait for a safe gap and then accelerate to merge with traffic.

question: When parking on any hill, you should:
options: a:Have one of your rear wheels touching the curb.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park".,c:Always point your front wheels parallel to the road even if there is a curb.
note: When parked on a hill, leave the vehicle in gear or in "park" and set the parking brake; turn wheels appropriately to prevent rolling if brakes fail.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid heavy braking.,b:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,c:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as possible.
note: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator to slow naturally, and use the brakes gently to come to a controlled stop.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings.,b:Watch for multiple trains.,c:Both of the above.
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution, be alert for vehicles that must stop, and watch for trains from either direction.

question: If you are about to be struck from behind, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Press your head firmly against the head restraint.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Applying your brakes if needed.
note: If hit from behind, keep a firm grip on the wheel and brace against the seat and head restraint; do not release the steering wheel.

question: What is the best general attitude when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.,b:Slightly increase your speed.,c:Expect the unexpected.
note: Construction zones often present unusual or changing conditions; drive with extreme caution for your safety and the workers' safety.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning in rain, you should:
options: a:Drive at speeds suitable for ideal conditions.,b:Apply your brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: Lower your speed in wet conditions to allow tires to channel water away from the tread and maintain road contact.

question: Your vehicle may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:35 miles per hour.,c:40 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds around 35 mph when standing water prevents the tire tread from contacting the road.

question: What should you do in inclement weather when steering and braking?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Drive in a low gear regardless of conditions.
note: Avoid sudden steering or braking movements in bad weather; smooth inputs help maintain traction and control.

question: When must motorists stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
options: a:All students are off the bus.,b:The stop arm is retracted.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: Vehicles must stop and remain stopped until the bus retracts its stop arm, turns off flashing red lights, and begins moving again.

question: A lane-control sign showing an arrow with the word "ONLY" means you must:
options: a:Travel in the direction of the arrow.,b:Always change lanes before proceeding.,c:Look for a destination sign to follow.
note: Lane-control signs indicate the required movement from that lane; follow the arrow direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Slow down and cross with caution.,b:Stop and wait for green.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light signals caution; slow, look for hazards, and proceed when safe, watching for pedestrians and other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means you should:
options: a:Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.,b:Assume no signal is needed from your lane.,c:Prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow indicates the protective turning time is ending; yield to oncoming traffic and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into your lane?
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,c:When you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: Only move back into your lane when you can see the other vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror, indicating sufficient space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking facing downhill on a hill, you should:
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road (toward the curb).,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Keep your wheels straight.
note: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding to the left, which way should you steer?
options: a:Steer left to follow the skid and regain control.,b:Steer right to counter the skid.,c:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: To recover from a skid, steer in the direction you want the car to go—if the rear slides left, steer left to align the vehicle.

question: A broken yellow centerline between two lanes indicates what?
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and means passing is allowed if it can be done safely and no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: Directions from a police officer override traffic signals and signs; follow the officer's instructions.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline prohibits passing; it indicates it is unsafe to overtake.

question: Streets and highways are most slippery:
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:Just after it starts to rain.
note: Road surfaces are especially slick during the first half hour of rain as water mixes with oil and residues on the pavement.

question: Which statement about driving while taking medications is correct?
options: a:Over-the-counter medicines are always safe at recommended doses.,b:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,c:All medications are safe if taken with food.,d:Prescription medicines never affect driving ability.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving; many cold and allergy medicines cause drowsiness.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Treat the light like a stop sign.,b:Continue through the intersection without stopping.,c:Wait until the light turns green to proceed.
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

question: To check areas your mirrors don't show, you should look:
options: a:Over your shoulders into your blind spots.,b:Only in the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only in the outside mirrors.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors; turning your head and glancing over your shoulder confirms the lane is clear.

question: What qualifies as a distraction while driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.
note: A distraction can be any activity or event that diverts your eyes, hands, or attention from driving, increasing crash risk.

question: What is an effective way to practice defensive driving?
options: a:Scan the road ahead.,b:Rubberneck.,c:Stare straight ahead.
note: Constantly scanning ahead and around your vehicle helps you spot hazards early and react safely.

question: If the highway marking is a single broken white line between lanes, you may:
options: a:Cross the line to pass or change lanes when safe.,b:Not cross the line to pass.,c:Only cross it if you are in the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed for passing or lane changes when safe.

question: How must you treat an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic or pedestrians, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, check for traffic, and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way only.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection without stopping.
note: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: If the centerline is one solid yellow and one broken yellow next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.,b:You are in a passing zone and may pass left if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:You are not allowed to pass in this area.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present; a solid line prohibits passing from the other side.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while driving helps you:
options: a:Keep up with traffic.,b:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Scanning far ahead helps avoid sudden maneuvers, saves fuel, and helps traffic flow smoothly.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn and the bus moves.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if you don't see children.,c:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and its stop arm is extended, all motorists must stop until the arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,b:They do not follow the same traffic rules as cars.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly, so tailgating greatly increases the likelihood of a rear-end collision with a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is not a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.,b:Change lanes without signaling.,c:Slower traffic must keep to the right.
note: Always signal before changing lanes. On interstates, slower traffic should stay to the right, and if you miss an exit, continue to the next one.

question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with a blood alcohol concentration of:
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount.
note: Arkansas enforces zero tolerance for under-21 drivers: any detectable alcohol can result in license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another vehicle is simply in your way.,c:To scold a driver who made a mistake.
note: Use the horn only to warn others of danger or to prevent a crash; avoid using it for impatience or punishment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start reducing speed?
options: a:As you approach the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then reduce speed to the exit ramp’s advisory speed.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:They increase as vehicle speed increases.,b:They decrease as speed increases.,c:They are not affected by speed.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and increase the severity of collisions; speed greatly affects crash outcomes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It notifies other road users of your intended action.,b:It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,c:Because it is always unsafe to turn off a signal early.
note: Continuous signaling lets drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions, reducing confusion and crashes.

question: When are you allowed to cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.,b:When the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.,c:When the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.
note: You may cross centerlines to pass only if the broken line is on your side and it is safe to do so.

question: As you near the crest of a hill, you should:
options: a:Be prepared to stop if necessary.,b:Speed up slightly to crest the hill quickly.,c:Maintain your exact speed without adjustment.
note: You may not be able to see hazards over the hill, so slow enough to stop if a stalled vehicle or obstacle appears.

question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Pass the area carefully and avoid slowing down to look at the activity.,b:Stop to watch the workers if curious.,c:Decrease your following distance to get through faster.
note: Don't "rubberneck"—maintain a safe speed and following distance and obey posted signs to keep workers and drivers safe.

question: In Arkansas, wearing a seat belt in the front passenger seat is:
options: a:Optional.,b:Required by law.,c:Suggested.
note: Arkansas law requires drivers and front-seat passengers to wear seat belts. Always buckle up.

question: What is the message on a red octagon-shaped traffic sign?
options: a:One-way.,b:Do not enter.,c:Stop.
note: An octagonal eight-sided red sign always means STOP; come to a full stop at the sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not yet entered, you should:
options: a:Reduce speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Come to a safe stop.,d:Stop only if pedestrians are crossing.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal will turn red; if you have not entered, prepare to stop safely.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible via your mirrors; always check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not working, what should you do when approaching the intersection?
options: a:If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.,b:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: Treat an inoperative signal as an all-way stop: stop, then yield the right-of-way as required before entering.

question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road, set the parking brake.,b:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Leave your wheels straight.
note: On an uphill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the road edge so if the vehicle rolls it will roll off the traveled way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should:
options: a:Turn into the first lane available on the one-way street.,b:Turn into any lane you choose.,c:Turn into the second lane over.
note: Turn from the lane nearest the centerline into the first legal lane of the one-way street to complete the turn safely.

question: When approaching a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.,b:Honk your horn to alert them and proceed, c:Carefully drive around them if possible.
note: Always yield to blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog and wait until they have cleared your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red arrow pointing right on a traffic signal means you may:
options: a:Turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Turn only after you come to a complete stop.,c:Not turn in that direction until the light changes to green.
note: A red arrow indicates you must stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears; do not turn against a red arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permitted to drive off the paved road to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You may not leave the paved or main-traveled portion of the road to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In traffic moving 50–55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:When you stay within that speed range with the flow of traffic.,b:When you drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,c:When you drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.
note: Traveling at a speed consistent with other vehicles (within posted limits) reduces speed differentials that often cause crashes.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, use which lights?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Low beam headlights reduce glare in fog, rain, or snow and make your vehicle more visible to others; high beams can worsen glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from an on-ramp, you should:
options: a:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,b:Merge into traffic without checking for cars.,c:Check for cars, increase speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.,d:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and merge smoothly when it is safe; do not stop on the ramp unless necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a one-way, multi-lane street onto another one-way street, you should begin the turn from which lane?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane as long as it seems safe.,c:The center lane of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto a one-way street, start the turn from the far left lane unless signs or markings indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the shoulder is wide enough.,b:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; other drivers will not expect you there.

question: Work zone barriers, barrels, cones, and signs are intended to:
options: a:Make drivers annoyed about slow traffic.,b:Inconvenience drivers.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work areas.
note: These devices are used to direct traffic safely away from work areas and alert drivers to hazards.
